mainTopic: Dividing a disputed item's value, and whether lifting a found item for a friend acquires it for him (רמי בר חמא vs. רבא).
overview: This amud opens by asking whether two people who split a disputed item really cut it in half. A plain טלית can still clothe small children, and a gold-threaded one can still clothe the children of kings. But a non-kosher animal would be ruined if cut, so the גמרא concludes that 'dividing' means splitting the item's value. Next, רמי בר חמא learns from the משנה that if you lift a found item for a friend, the friend acquires it. רבא disagrees: in the משנה each person acquires for himself, and because of that he also acquires for the other (מגו דזכי לנפשיה זכי נמי לחבריה). רבא proves this from partners who steal together. The גמרא then works through רבא's ruling about a חרש and a פקח who lift an item together, and concludes that neither acquires. Then רב אחא asks which line of the משנה רמי בר חמא used. After several lines are tried and rejected, the last clause about dividing without an oath is offered, though רבא explains it through his מגו. The amud ends as רב יוסף begins a teaching from רב יהודה about two riding an animal; the teaching itself continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The cut garment is still useful for small children
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: cutting the טלית in half does not ruin it, because the halves can still be used for children's clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is still fit for small children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer that began before this section. Cutting the disputed טלית in two is allowed, because each half can still be made into a garment for a small child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that splitting the טלית destroys it, so nobody really gains anything. The answer is that a half-garment still has real value, since it can clothe a child. So the claimants can actually cut it and each take a piece.

phrases.english: Because it is fit for small children.
phrases.notes: He means each half of the cut טלית can still be sewn into a garment for a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that started earlier on the daf, about whether the טלית itself is physically divided.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the divided object keeps real value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting the טלית would ruin it, so it cannot really be divided.
steps.terutzMaskana: The halves are still usable for children's clothing, so physical division is allowed.

steps.title: What about רבא's gold-threaded garment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of physically cutting the item, using רבא's ruling about a טלית woven with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said: if the טלית was woven with gold, they split it. Do they really cut that one too? Doing that would ruin it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. רבא ruled that a gold-threaded טלית is also split, but cutting such a fancy garment seems to destroy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain טלית can be turned into children's clothes. A gold-threaded garment is a luxury item, though, and cutting it seems to wreck its value. So does physical division still work here?

keyTerms.meaning: A garment woven with gold thread
Does it also mean that / so too

phrases.english: But that which רבא said:
If the garment was woven with gold, they divide it,
does that also mean they cut it up?
But they would be ruining it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer from step 1 on a harder case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the disputed garment is physically cut in half.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gold-threaded garment loses its value when cut, so physical division seems impossible.

steps.title: Gold-threaded halves suit royal children
steps.stepSummary: The halves of the gold garment can still clothe the children of kings, so it is not ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is no problem, because it is fit for the children of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even a cut gold-threaded garment can be made into clothing for royal or wealthy children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reasoning from step 1 is extended upward. A small fancy garment still has a fancy buyer, namely the children of kings. So physical division still makes sense.

phrases.english: That is not difficult,
because it is fit for the children of kings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the same logic: the divided item still has a suitable user.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting a gold garment ruins it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It stays valuable as clothing for royal children, so it can be cut.

steps.title: What about the two riders on one animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges physical division again, using the משנה's case of two people riding one animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: if two people were riding on an animal, and so on. Do they really cut the animal up too? That would ruin it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new and stronger challenge from the משנה at the start of the פרק. There, two riders each claim an animal and split it, and cutting up an animal seems to ruin it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'dividing' always means physically cutting, then the animal case would require killing and cutting the animal. That seems to destroy what both people are fighting over.

keyTerms.meaning: That we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: But that which we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה וְכוּ׳,
phrases.english: If two were riding on an animal, and so on,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 2a. The 'and so on' points to the rest of it: each claims the whole animal, and they divide.

phrases.english: does that also mean they cut it up?
But they would be ruining it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the garment cases survived, the גמרא tests the idea on an animal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that 'they divide' means physically splitting the object.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting a living animal in half destroys it.

steps.title: A kosher animal is fine, but a non-kosher one is ruined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. A kosher animal could be slaughtered and split for meat, but a non-kosher animal would be worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for a kosher animal, which is fit for meat. But a non-kosher animal would be ruined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the problem. It admits a kosher animal could be slaughtered and the meat shared, but a non-kosher animal has no such use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the last escape route. For a non-kosher animal, cutting it destroys its value completely, and the משנה makes no distinction between animals. So physical division cannot be what the משנה means.

phrases.english: It works for a kosher animal, which is fit for meat.
But a non-kosher animal would be ruined!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the challenge of step 4 by removing the kosher-meat answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: Physical division in the animal case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A non-kosher animal has no use once cut, so splitting it destroys everything.

steps.title: They divide the value, not the object
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'dividing' means splitting the money value, and applies this to the garment cases too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they divide its value. Here too, they divide its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that in the animal case they split its monetary value. It then says the same is true in the earlier garment cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'still useful' answers from steps 1 and 3 are now set aside. Since the animal case can only mean dividing value, 'they divide' in the other cases is read the same way. Nobody actually cuts anything; they share what it is worth.
steps.whatToRemember: When the משנה says disputing claimants 'divide' an item, it means they split its monetary value, not the physical object.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the garment is still physically cut because of the 'children' answers. The final word, 'here too, its value,' replaces that approach.

phrases.english: Rather, they divide its value,
here too, they divide its value.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the garment cases discussed earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 4-5 and applies the answer back to the garment cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In all these cases, the claimants divide the item's monetary value.

steps.title: Lifting a found item for someone else
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא learns from the משנה that if you lift a found item for a friend, the friend acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: This tells us that if someone lifts a found item for his friend, the friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רמי בר חמא draws a rule from the משנה about acquiring a lost item through someone else's lifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting an object (הגבהה) is a way of acquiring it. רמי בר חמא says the משנה shows this act can work for another person, so the friend becomes the owner. The גמרא will next explain how he sees this in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lifts (a way of acquiring)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the topic of acquiring for someone else through lifting, which the גמרא goes on to discuss and question.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
This tells us,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה on 2a. He is drawing a lesson from it.

phrases.english: one who lifts a found item for his friend,
his friend acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, drawn from the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifting a found item on behalf of another person makes that other person the owner.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's proof from the two people holding the garment
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא explains his proof. If lifting for a friend did not work, neither holder in the משנה would acquire the garment. Since the משנה says they split it, lifting for a friend must work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the friend does not acquire, then each half should be treated as if it is still lying on the ground, and neither person should get anything. So we must learn that if you lift a found item for a friend, the friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא is proving his rule from step 7. He shows that the משנה only makes sense if lifting for a friend really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people hold the garment together, so neither one lifts the whole thing by himself. Each one is partly lifting it for the other. If that kind of lifting did not count, it would be as if nobody lifted it, and the משנה could not tell them to divide it.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind (an idea the גמרא is about to reject)
Lying on the ground (not yet acquired by anyone)
Learn from it (a conclusion is drawn)
One who lifts a found item for his friend

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that the friend does not acquire,

phrases.aramaic: תֵּיעָשֶׂה זוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁמּוּנַּחַת עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: then this part should be treated as if it is lying on the ground,

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁמּוּנַּחַת עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: and that part as if it is lying on the ground,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִקְנֶה לֹא זֶה וְלֹא זֶה.
phrases.english: and neither this one nor that one should acquire it.
Rather, isn't it right to learn from it:
one who lifts a found item for his friend, the friend acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לֹא קָנָה חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning behind רמי בר חמא's inference from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who lifts a found item for a friend makes the friend acquire it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two people holding a garment, where the משנה rules that they divide it.

steps.title: רבא rejects the proof and explains the case through מגו
steps.stepSummary: רבא says lifting for a friend may not work at all. In the משנה each person acquires for himself, and because of that he can also acquire for the other person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, I can say that one who lifts a found item for his friend does not make the friend acquire it. Here the reason is: since he acquires for himself, he also acquires for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רמי בר חמא's proof. He gives a different reason why the two holders in the משנה acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא assumed the משנה proves that lifting purely for someone else works. רבא says the משנה is a special case. Each holder is also acquiring for himself, and that personal acquisition lets him acquire for the other person too. So the משנה tells us nothing about lifting only for a friend.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (keeping the original position despite the proof)
Since (one thing works, a related thing works too)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying lifting for a friend works. He says it does NOT work on its own. It only works here because the lifter is also acquiring for himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the principle of מגו דזכי לנפשיה זכי נמי לחבריה, which the rest of the section builds on.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Really, I can say to you:
one who lifts a found item for his friend,
the friend does not acquire it.
And here, this is the reason:
phrases.notes: "Here" means the משנה of the two people holding the garment.

phrases.english: since he acquires for himself,
he also acquires for his friend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 8 by offering another reason for the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה, not necessarily רמי בר חמא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's case involves someone who also acquires for himself, so it cannot prove what happens when you lift only for someone else.

steps.title: Proof for מגו from partners who steal together
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his principle. A person who sends an agent to steal is exempt. But partners who steal are both liable. This must be because the one who takes the item acquires for himself and therefore also for his partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know this: if someone says to his agent, "Go out and steal for me," and he steals, the sender is exempt. But partners who stole are both liable. What is the reason? Isn't it because we say that since he acquires for himself, he also acquires for his friend? Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a case from the laws of theft to prove that his מגו principle is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, one person cannot make someone else responsible by stealing for him, so the sender is exempt. Yet with partners, both are liable even though one did the taking. The only explanation is that the partner took the item for himself, and so he also acquired it for his partner.

keyTerms.meaning: Agent, someone sent to act for another

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: someone acting purely for another does not acquire for him. But someone who acquires for himself also acquires for his partner (מגו דזכי לנפשיה זכי נמי לחבריה).

phrases.english: Know this, for if one said to his agent:
"Go out and steal for me," and he stole, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The one who is exempt is the sender, not the agent who actually stole.

phrases.english: But partners who stole are liable.
What is the reason?
Is it not because we say:

phrases.aramaic: מִגּוֹ דְּזָכֵי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ זָכֵי נָמֵי לְחַבְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: since he acquires for himself, he also acquires for his friend?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides evidence for the מגו principle that רבא introduced in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The principle מגו דזכי לנפשיה זכי נמי לחבריה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between a sender of an agent to steal, who is exempt, and partners who steal, who are both liable.

steps.title: Applying מגו to a deaf-mute and a competent person who lift together
steps.stepSummary: רבא draws a new ruling from his principle. When a חרש and a פקח lift a found item together, since the חרש acquires, the פקח acquires too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that you said we use the idea of "since" (מגו), a deaf-mute and a competent person who lifted a found item together: since the deaf-mute acquires, the competent person acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the מגו principle he just proved and applies it to a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case pairs a חרש, whose ability to acquire is weaker in הלכה, with a פקח, who can acquire normally. רבא says they work together like the partners. The one's acquisition carries the other along.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you said (building a new ruling on an accepted one)
A deaf-mute, treated in halacha as lacking full legal understanding
Since, because of (same idea as מגו)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now that you said that we say "since":
a deaf-mute and a competent person who lifted a found item together,
since the deaf-mute acquires, the competent person acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ אָמְרִינַן מִגּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new practical ruling on the מגו principle that was proven in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a חרש and a פקח lift a found item together, the חרש's acquisition lets the פקח acquire as well.

steps.title: How Can the Competent Person Acquire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the חרש acquires through the פקח's lifting, but asks how the פקח himself acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the חרש acquires, because a competent person lifted the item for him. But how does the פקח acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling from step 11. One half of it makes sense, but the other half does not seem to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using רבא's own principle, the פקח acquires for himself and so can acquire the other side for the חרש. But for the פקח to get the other side, the חרש would have to acquire it for him, and a חרש cannot acquire for anyone else. So the 'both acquire' ruling breaks down on the פקח's side.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, treated in הלכה as lacking legal understanding

phrases.english: Granted, the deaf-mute acquires,
because a competent person is lifting it for him.
But the competent person, by what does he acquire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling רבא gave in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that both the חרש and the פקח acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's principle works only for someone who acquires for himself. The חרש cannot acquire, so he cannot pass a share to the פקח.

steps.title: Rereading רבא: Only the Deaf-Mute Acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבא as saying the חרש acquires and the פקח does not. The 'since' is that two חרשים acquire when they lift an item together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: the חרש acquires and the פקח does not. And what is the 'since'? Since two חרשים in general acquire, this חרש also acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by changing how we read רבא's ruling. Now only the חרש acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מגו no longer means 'he acquires for himself, so he acquires for his partner.' It now means that a חרש lifting together with another חרש would acquire, so he also acquires when lifting with a פקח. The פקח gets nothing, which solves the problem from step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of (an argument built on another case)
In general / in an ordinary case

steps.confusionAlert: The word מגו here is not the same argument רבא used in step 9. Here it compares this חרש to two חרשים lifting together. It does not mean the פקח acquires for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: חֵרֵשׁ – קָנָה, פִּקֵּחַ – לָא קָנָה.
phrases.english: Rather, say: the deaf-mute acquires, the competent person does not acquire.
And what is the "since"?
Since two deaf-mutes in general acquire,
this one too acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: חֵרֵשׁ – קָנָה, פִּקֵּחַ – לָא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12 by rereading רבא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ruling (אֶלָּא אֵימָא) and giving the word מגו a new meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the חרש and the פקח acquire, because each acquires for himself and so for the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the חרש acquires, based on the case of two חרשים lifting together.

steps.title: The Competent Person Lifted Only for Himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the new reading. Lifting for a friend works only when you mean it for the friend. The פקח lifted for himself, and if he does not acquire, he cannot acquire for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? Even if you say that someone who lifts a found item for his friend makes the friend acquire, that applies when he lifts it with his friend in mind. This פקח lifted it with himself in mind. If he himself does not acquire, can he acquire for others?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from step 13. That reading leaves the חרש acquiring through a פקח who acquired nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש cannot acquire on his own, so his share must come from the פקח's lifting. Even רמי בר חמא's rule only works when the lifter means to acquire for the other person. Here the פקח meant to acquire only for himself and failed, so his lifting cannot give anything to the חרש.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (introduces a strong objection)
Even if you say / even if you accept

phrases.english: What is this?
Even if you say
one who lifts a found item for his friend, his friend acquires,
phrases.notes: This is רמי בר חמא's rule from step 7.

phrases.english: that applies

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּקָא מַגְבַּהּ לֵיהּ אַדַּעְתָּא דְּחַבְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: where he lifts it with his friend in mind.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אַדַּעְתָּא דִּידֵיהּ קָא מַגְבַּהּ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: This one lifts it with himself in mind,
he himself does not acquire, and he makes others acquire?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading of רבא given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the חרש acquires while the פקח does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חרש's share can only come through the פקח's lifting. That lifting was meant for the פקח himself and failed, so it cannot give anything to the חרש.

steps.title: Since the Competent Person Does Not Acquire, Neither Does the Deaf-Mute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבא's ruling a final time: because the פקח does not acquire, the חרש does not acquire either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: since the פקח does not acquire, the חרש does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final reading of רבא's ruling, which answers the problem from step 14. In this case neither person acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed the פקח cannot acquire, since a חרש cannot acquire for him. Step 14 showed the חרש's share depends on the פקח. So when the פקח fails, the חרש fails too, and neither one acquires the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of (the Hebrew form of מִגּוֹ)

steps.whatToRemember: When a חרש and a פקח lift a found item together, the final reading of רבא is that neither acquires. The פקח cannot get a share through the חרש, and the חרש's share depended on the פקח.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא קָנָה פִּקֵּחַ –
phrases.english: Rather, say: since the competent person did not acquire,
the deaf-mute did not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא קָנָה פִּקֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14 with a final reading of רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ruling (אֶלָּא אֵימָא) to reach the opposite result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חרש acquires even though the פקח does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither acquires. The חרש's share fails because the פקח's lifting gave him nothing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רבא's case of a חרש and a פקח lifting together, neither one acquires.

steps.title: Why is this different from two deaf people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question in advance: two חרשים who lift together do acquire, so why does a חרש lose out here?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will ask: how is this different from the ordinary case of two deaf people who find something together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא predicts a question someone might ask about the conclusion in Step 15. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 ruled that when a חרש and a פקח lift together, neither acquires. But two חרשים lifting together do acquire. If a חרש can acquire alongside another חרש, why not alongside a פקח?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a way of raising an expected question)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
How is this different from the ordinary case of two deaf-mutes?
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 13, where two חרשים lifting together do acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מַאי שְׁנָא מִשְּׁנֵי חֵרְשִׁין דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible objection to the final reading of רבא in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a חרש lifting with a פקח does not acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two חרשים acquire when they lift together. So a חרש should be able to acquire with a פקח as well.

steps.title: The enactment for deaf people exists to prevent fights
steps.stepSummary: Two חרשים acquire only because the רבנן enacted it to prevent quarrels. A חרש next to a פקח who did not acquire would not quarrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the רבנן made an enactment for them so they would not come to fight. Here, the חרש says to himself: if the פקח doesn't get it, should I get it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 16. The rule for חרשים is a special enactment of the רבנן, and its reason does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש normally cannot acquire on his own. The רבנן gave him acquisition anyway so that people would not fight with him over items. When he sees that even the פקח did not acquire, he will not fight, so the enactment is not needed.
steps.whatToRemember: Two חרשים acquire only because of a rabbinic enactment to prevent fights. When no fight is expected, as with a חרש beside a פקח, the enactment does not apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rabbinic enactment reaches only as far as its reason does.

phrases.english: There, the Rabbis made an enactment for them
so that they will not come to quarrel.
Here, he says to himself:
The competent man does not acquire, and I should acquire?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם תַּקִּינוּ לְהוּ רַבָּנַן דְּלָא אָתֵי לְאִנְּצוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the reason behind the enactment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since two חרשים acquire together, a חרש should also acquire together with a פקח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The enactment for חרשים exists only to prevent fights. A חרש beside a פקח who did not acquire will not fight, so he does not acquire.

steps.title: Where did רמי בר חמא learn his rule?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אדא asks רב אשי which part of the משנה is the source of רמי בר חמא's inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב אדא said to רב אשי: רמי בר חמא's inference, where does it come from?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב אחא wants to know exactly which words of the משנה רמי בר חמא used for his rule about lifting a found item for a friend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רמי בר חמא learned from our משנה that someone who lifts a found item for a friend acquires it for the friend. Now the גמרא tests whether that rule really comes out of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: His inference, what he learned from the precise wording
The אמורא who learned the rule from the משנה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Adda, said to Rav Ashi:
Rami bar Chama's inference, from where is it?
phrases.notes: His inference is the rule from Step 7: one who lifts a found item for his friend, the friend acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, asking for the source of רמי בר חמא's earlier inference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה רמי בר חמא used to learn that lifting for a friend acquires for the friend.

steps.title: The garment case cannot be the source
steps.stepSummary: The first case of the משנה cannot be the source, because there each person claims he lifted the whole garment for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it comes from the first case, 'two are holding a garment,' there this one says 'it's all mine and I lifted all of it,' and that one says 'it's all mine and I lifted all of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opening case of the משנה as the source and rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the garment case, each person claims he lifted the entire garment for himself. Nobody is lifting anything for someone else, so the case cannot teach a rule about lifting for a friend.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: If we say from the first clause,
"Two are holding a garment,"
there, this one is saying
"All of it is mine, and I lifted all of it,"
and that one says
"All of it is mine, and I lifted all of it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries one possible answer to Step 18 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the opening garment case as the source of רמי בר חמא's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case each person claims to have lifted the whole garment for himself. Nothing there involves lifting for another person.

steps.title: The source is an extra line in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The line 'this one says all of it is mine' seems unnecessary. So it must be teaching that lifting for a friend acquires for the friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from what the משנה teaches: 'this one says it's all mine and that one says it's all mine.' Why do I need this too? Rather, learn from the extra line: one who lifts a found item for his friend, the friend acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. רמי בר חמא learned his rule from a line of the משנה that looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said 'this one says I found it,' so repeating the claim 'all of it is mine' seems unnecessary. A line that seems extra must be there to teach something new. Here, that new thing is that lifting a found item for a friend acquires it for the friend.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this as well?
An extra, seemingly unnecessary line in the משנה
One who lifts a found item for his friend

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lines. The source is NOT the garment case of Step 19. It is the second line about claims, 'this one says all of it is mine.'

phrases.english: Rather, from what is taught:
"This one says all of it is mine
and that one says all of it is mine"
Why do I need this as well?
Rather, learn from the extra line of the משנה:
One who lifts a found item for his friend, his friend acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the garment case was ruled out in Step 19, offers the extra line as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רמי בר חמא learned his rule from the seemingly extra line 'this one says all of it is mine and that one says all of it is mine.'

steps.title: But that line was already explained as buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The line is not extra after all. The גמרא already explained that the first clause is about a found item and the second is about a purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already explain that the first part is about a found item, and the last part is about buying and selling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 20, saying the line is not extra at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the מסכתא, the גמרא explained that 'I found it' is about a found item, while 'all of it is mine' is about two people who each claim they bought the item. So the second line has its own case and is not extra. That means it cannot be used to teach רמי בר חמא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We established, we explained it as
The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: But didn't we establish the first clause as about a found item,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the explanation at the start of the מסכתא, on דף ב.

phrases.english: and the last clause as about buying and selling!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אוֹקֵימְנָא רֵישָׁא בִּמְצִיאָה, וְסֵיפָא בְּמִקָּח וּמִמְכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 20 that the line is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'this one says all of it is mine' is an extra line.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That line was already explained as a separate case about buying and selling. So it is not extra and cannot be the source of רמי בר חמא's rule.

steps.title: A new source: the 'all versus half' clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now proposes that רמי בר חמא learned his rule from the latter clause of the משנה, where one says 'all is mine' and the other says 'half is mine.' That clause seems extra, so it must teach that lifting for a friend acquires for the friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is the latter clause: 'This one says all of it is mine and that one says half of it is mine.' Why do I need this as well? Rather, learn from this extra line in the משנה: one who lifts a found item for his friend, the friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous try failed, so the גמרא offers a new answer. It says the source is the latter clause, where one claims all and the other claims half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא argues that the 'all versus half' case adds nothing new. When a line in the משנה looks unneeded, we read it as teaching something else. Here, that something else is רמי בר חמא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
An extra, seemingly unneeded line in the משנה
One who lifts a found item on behalf of his friend

phrases.english: Rather, from the latter clause:
"This one says all of it is mine
and that one says half of it is mine,"
why do I need this as well?
Rather, from the extra line in the משנה, learn from it:
one who lifts a found item for his friend,
his friend acquires it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 21 with a new proposed source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'all versus half' clause is extra, so it teaches that one who lifts for his friend acquires for the friend.

steps.title: Maybe this clause is about a purchase
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new source. Who says the latter clause is about a found item? It may be about buying and selling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you know it is about a found item? Perhaps it is about buying and selling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just gave. The 'all versus half' clause might be about a purchase and not about a found item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא's rule is about a found item. If this clause is about a purchase, it cannot teach a rule about lifting a found item for a friend.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do you know it is about a found item?
Perhaps it is about buying and selling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from step 22 by questioning what kind of case the clause describes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'all versus half' clause is about a found item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the clause is about a purchase, it says nothing about acquiring a found item for a friend.

steps.title: But a purchase reading would add nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a defense of the proof. If the clause were about a purchase, what would it be teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: if it is about buying and selling, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone defending the proof. That person says the purchase reading leaves the line with no point, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense is that a line must teach something. If reading it as a purchase makes it empty, then it must be about a found item after all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it?

phrases.english: And if you would say:
if it is about buying and selling,
what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argues that the alternative reading would leave the line with no purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause might be about a purchase.
steps.terutzMaskana: A purchase reading would teach nothing, so the clause must be about a found item.

steps.title: The purchase reading does teach something: the crafty claimant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the defense. Even as a purchase, the clause teaches that the one who claims half is not treated like someone returning a lost item, because he may be using a trick to avoid an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought the one who says 'half is mine' is like someone returning a lost item and should be exempt. So the משנה teaches that he is being crafty. He thinks: if I say 'all of it is mine,' I will have to swear. I will say this instead, so I will look like someone returning a lost item and be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the clause has its own lesson even if it is about a purchase. So the clause is not extra, and the proof for רמי בר חמא falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think that by giving up half, the claimant acts like an honest person returning a lost item, and so he skips the oath. The משנה teaches that he still swears, because he may have given up half only to avoid swearing. Since the line has this lesson, it is not extra and cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say
One who returns a lost item
He is acting craftily, using a trick

steps.whatToRemember: The 'all versus half' clause is not extra. Even as a purchase case, it teaches that the half-claimer still swears, so it cannot be the source for רמי בר חמא.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
for it would enter your mind to say
that this one who says "half of it is mine"
should be like one returning a lost item and be exempt.
phrases.notes: Exempt means he would not have to take the oath.

phrases.english: So it teaches us
that this one is acting craftily.
He thinks: if I say "all of it is mine,"
I will need to swear;
I will say this instead,
so that I will be like one returning a lost item and be exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense in step 24, which brings down the proof from step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the 'all versus half' clause
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The clause is not extra. As a purchase case, it teaches that the half-claimer is not treated like one returning a lost item.

steps.title: Another proposed source: two riding on an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now proposes the case of two people riding on an animal as the source. That case seems extra, so it teaches that one who lifts a found item for his friend acquires it for the friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is this: 'If two were riding on an animal.' Why do I need this as well? Rather, learn from this extra line in the משנה: one who lifts a found item for his friend, the friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: After the previous try failed, the גמרא points to a different line in the משנה, the case of two riders on one animal. It suggests this line is the extra one that teaches רמי בר חמא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא uses the same method as before: find a line that adds nothing new and read the rule into it. This time the line is the riders case.
steps.whatToRemember: This proposed source does not hold up. The next step shows that the riding case has its own lesson, so it is not extra.

phrases.english: Rather, from this:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: "If two were riding on an animal,"
why do I need this as well?
Rather, from the extra line in the משנה, learn from it:
one who lifts a found item for his friend,
his friend acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָא, הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 25 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of two riding on an animal is extra, so it teaches that one who lifts for his friend acquires for the friend.

steps.title: The riding case may teach that a rider acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the case of two riding an animal. That case is not extra, because it may be teaching that a rider also acquires the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the case teaches us that one who rides on an animal also acquires it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 26 by showing that the riding case has its own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said the riding case was extra, so it must teach רמי בר חמא's rule. The גמרא answers that it is not extra. It teaches something new: a רוכב (rider) acquires, not only one who leads the animal. Once the case has its own purpose, it is no longer a proof for רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; it introduces another way to read the source
This is what it teaches us
One who rides or sits on an animal

phrases.english: But perhaps this is what it teaches us:
that one who rides also acquires!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא, הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן דְּרוֹכֵב נָמֵי קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed source from Step 26
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the riding case for רמי בר חמא's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is not extra. It has its own lesson, that a rider acquires.

steps.title: New source: dividing without an oath when they admit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes the משנה's last clause as the source. When the two admit or have witnesses, they divide without an oath. For a purchase this would be obvious, so it must be about a found item, which shows that lifting for a friend acquires for the friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from the last clause: When they admit, or when they have witnesses, they divide without an oath. What case is this? If it is buying and selling, does it need to be said? Rather, it must be about a found item. Learn from it that one who lifts a found item for his friend acquires it for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new source for רמי בר חמא's rule, the clause about two people who admit or have witnesses and divide without an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two people bought something together and agree on that, of course they split it. Saying so would teach nothing. So the clause must be about a found item that they lifted together. That means each one lifted part of it for the other, and the other acquired it. This is רמי בר חמא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה
They admit, meaning each agrees to the other's claim
They divide without taking an oath
Does it need to be said? Meaning it is obvious

phrases.english: Rather, from the last clause:
When they admit
or when they have witnesses,
they divide without an oath.
What case is this?
If it is buying and selling, does it need to be said?!
Rather, is it not about a found item?
And learn from it
that one who lifts a found item for his friend,
his friend acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִסֵּיפָא: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מוֹדִין אוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the riding case was rejected, offers a new source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause about admitting or having witnesses must be about a found item. So lifting for a friend acquires for the friend.

steps.title: רבא: acquiring for the friend works because he also acquires for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the clause another way. Each one acquires for himself, and because of that he can also acquire for his friend. This does not prove that lifting only for a friend works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא would tell you: Since he acquires for himself, he also acquires for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבא, who disagrees with רמי בר חמא, would answer the proof from the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the found-item case, each person was lifting partly for himself. רבא says that because he is acquiring for himself, he can at the same time acquire for his friend. This is a מִגּוֹ. It does not show that someone lifting only for a friend acquires for the friend, so the clause is no proof for רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבא would tell you; this is how רבא would answer
Since; because one thing works, a related thing also works

steps.whatToRemember: The last clause (מודין או שיש להן עדים) stands as רמי בר חמא's source. רבא does not accept the proof. He explains the same clause through מִגּוֹ: acquiring for a friend works when he is also acquiring for himself.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying lifting for a friend always works. He says it works here only because each person was also acquiring for himself.

phrases.english: And רבא would say to you:
Since he acquires for himself,
he also acquires for his friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: מִגּוֹ דְּזָכֵי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ זָכֵי נָמֵי לְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבא rejects the proof from Step 28
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the last clause for רמי בר חמא's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case each person also acquires for himself. A מִגּוֹ explains why it works for the friend too, without proving the general rule.

steps.title: Opening the discussion of two riding on an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new section on the משנה's case of two people riding on an animal. רב יוסף introduces a teaching he heard from רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If two were riding on an animal. רב יוסף said: רב יהודה said to me:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to a new part of the משנה, the case of two riders. This line sets up a teaching by רב יהודה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search for the source of רמי בר חמא's rule is finished. The גמרא now quotes the משנה's riding case to discuss it directly. The words of רב יהודה's teaching come right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: If two were riding on an animal; the words of the משנה
An אמורא who reports the teaching
רב יוסף's teacher, the source of the teaching

phrases.english: If two were riding.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר לִי רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: רב יוסף said: רב יהודה said to me:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר לִי רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the source search ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רב יהודה's teaching on the משנה's case of two riding on an animal. The teaching itself comes next.
